findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher has inverted logic and wrong substring index, so it never validates the grant shortcut
findings.body: The new `isAccessTokenId` matcher contains `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` — two bugs. First, the condition is inverted: it returns false (no match) when the shortcut *equals* the expected value, so even with a correct index the matcher would reject valid tokens and accept wrong-grant tokens. Second, the index is wrong: the grant shortcut occupies characters 4-6 of the 6-char prefix (session type 0-2, token type 2-4, grant type 4-6), so it should be `substring(4, 6)`, not `substring(3, 5)` which extracts e.g. "ta" from "onrtac". Because of the wrong index, the equality check essentially never fires for real tokens, so `expectCodeToToken`, `expectRefresh`, `expectDeviceCodeToToken` and `expectAuthReqIdToToken` only assert that the ID has two colon-separated parts and the second is a UUID — the grant-type encoding added by this PR is completely unverified by the testsuite. Any regression in the token ID encoding would go unnoticed. Additionally, `items[0].substring(3, 5)` can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException for IDs with a shorter prefix instead of returning false.

findings.title: Constructor null-checks grantType twice; rawTokenId is never null-checked
findings.body: In the `AccessTokenContext` constructor, `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, ...)` is invoked twice (lines 72 and 73) and the second one is mislabeled "Null rawTokenId not allowed". The intended check for `rawTokenId` is missing, so an AccessTokenContext with a null rawTokenId can be constructed and will only fail later (e.g., NPE during string concatenation in `encodeTokenId`). Fix the second requireNonNull to check `rawTokenId`.

findings.title: New abstract method getShortcut() on the pluggable OAuth2GrantTypeFactory SPI breaks existing custom grant implementations
findings.body: `getShortcut()` was added as an abstract (non-default) method to the `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` interface in `server-spi-private`. OAuth 2.0 grant types are a deployable extension point (factories are registered via META-INF/services), so any existing third-party grant-type provider will fail to load/compile after upgrade with "does not define getShortcut()". To preserve compatibility, the method should have a sensible `default` implementation (e.g., deriving from the ID or returning a marker that the encoder maps to the UNKNOWN shortcut) instead of forcing every existing implementation to be updated.

findings.title: Public copy constructor OAuth2GrantType.Context(Context) was removed
findings.body: The public copy constructor `Context(Context context)` of the public static class `OAuth2GrantType.Context` was deleted as part of this change. This class lives in the `server-spi-private` grants package that custom grant-type implementations compile against; any external code that used the copy constructor will break at compile time on upgrade. The removal is not required by the rest of the change (the new `grantType` field could be copied along), so it should either be kept (also copying `grantType`, which would arguably be more correct than re-reading form params) or the break should be explicitly acknowledged.

findings.title: Decoder assumes fixed 2-character shortcuts but the SPI javadoc invites longer shortcuts, producing undecodable token IDs
findings.body: `getTokenContextFromTokenId` hard-requires the prefix before ':' to be exactly 6 characters (2 chars each for session type, token type and grant type) and throws `IllegalArgumentException` otherwise. However, `OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` is documented as "usually like 3-letters shortcut" with no length constraint, and third parties can implement it. A custom grant whose shortcut is not exactly 2 characters will encode fine (`encodeTokenId` just concatenates), but the resulting token ID (e.g., 7-char prefix) will be rejected by `getTokenContextFromTokenId` with an exception — tokens minted by Keycloak itself become undecodable. Either enforce/validate the 2-char length when populating the factory maps in `postInit`, or make the decoding format length-agnostic (e.g., split on fixed delimiters as in the original longer `st.on_tt.rt_gt.ac:` format).

findings.title: getTokenContextFromTokenId throws on any colon-containing but malformed/unknown prefix instead of degrading to UNKNOWN
findings.body: The decoder is lenient for legacy IDs without ':' (returns UNKNOWN context) but throws `IllegalArgumentException` for IDs that contain ':' with an unknown or wrong-length prefix. Since the token ID (`jti`) originates from externally presented tokens — e.g., tokens issued by another Keycloak deployment with a custom `TokenContextEncoderProvider` (the SPI explicitly exists to allow alternate encodings), a future format change, or foreign IDPs whose `jti` happens to contain a colon — any consumer of this method (introspection, userInfo, the planned session-lookup optimization from #37662) can be made to fail with a runtime exception by presenting an otherwise perfectly valid, signature-verified token. Decoding of a descriptive prefix should degrade gracefully to UNKNOWN (as already done for the no-colon case) rather than throw, since the encoded info is an optimization hint, not a security invariant.

findings.title: Duplicate-shortcut validation only runs at startup; late-registered grants can silently corrupt the shortcut maps
findings.body: `postInit` validates shortcut/ID uniqueness once by comparing map sizes, and `getShortcutByGrantType`/`getGrantTypeByShortcut` later add entries for grant factories not present at startup (comment: "in case new grant type was deployed") without re-checking for collisions. If a hot-deployed grant uses a shortcut (or ID) already mapped, `grantsByShortcuts.put(...)` silently overwrites the existing entry, so two distinct grant types map to the same shortcut and previously issued token IDs are misinterpreted (wrong grant type returned from `getTokenContextFromTokenId`). At minimum the lazy-population paths should detect the collision (e.g., refuse to overwrite an existing different mapping) instead of silently clobbering.

findings.title: testIncorrectGrantType catches bare RuntimeException and never asserts the exception type
findings.body: `testIncorrectGrantType` wraps the call in `try { ... } catch (RuntimeException iae) { }`, so the test passes for *any* runtime failure — including a `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` or NPE from an unrelated bug in the parsing code — not just the intended `IllegalArgumentException` about the unknown grant shortcut. It should assert the exception type (and ideally the message), e.g., `Assert.fail` in try and `catch (IllegalArgumentException e)` specifically. Also note the test relies on the 'ac' shortcut being absent from the hand-built maps, which makes it sensitive to map-setup drift rather than testing the real factory wiring; there is no test that exercises `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit` against the actual grant providers, nor any test of `getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext`.
